claims.text: Conventional melting, casting, or homogenization produces a largely uniform high-entropy-alloy microstructure without engineered nanoscale precipitates.
A tailored heat treatment can trigger controlled nucleation and growth of nanoscale coherent precipitates in a high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Optimizing temperature, time, and cooling rate can produce controlled precipitation without excessive coarsening or deleterious phases.
The treatment may not work when the alloy chemistry is unable to support the desired precipitate distribution.
Nanoscale precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Nanoscale precipitates provide sites for dislocation storage.
The combination of impeded dislocation motion and dislocation storage can balance strength and ductility.
Precipitate-induced local stress fields promote strain accommodation and thereby improve ductility.
A uniform precipitate dispersion improves load transfer through the material.
Improved load transfer increases or optimizes the effective Young’s modulus.
Uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates blunt crack propagation and increase fracture resistance.
The tailored heat treatment will improve yield strength relative to untreated homogeneous high-entropy alloys.
The tailored heat treatment will improve elongation at fracture relative to untreated homogeneous high-entropy alloys.
The tailored heat treatment will improve effective Young’s modulus relative to untreated homogeneous high-entropy alloys.
The tailored heat treatment will improve fracture toughness relative to untreated homogeneous high-entropy alloys.
Precipitate coarsening or brittle-phase formation can negate the expected mechanical-property improvements.
The magnitude of the property changes depends on alloy system and processing conditions.
